_meta.indication: Indicated in adults for the treatment of acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI) caused by susceptible isolates of designated Gram-positive and Gram-negative organisms.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized (1:1), double-blind trial comparing IV delafloxacin 300 mg q12h to vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h plus aztreonam 2 g q12h.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Objective response of >=20% reduction in lesion erythema vs baseline at 48 to 72 hours after initiation of therapy, with no evidence of clinical failure.
pivotal_trials.n: 660 randomized (331 IV delafloxacin, 329 vancomycin plus aztreonam).
pivotal_trials.result: Objective clinical response 259/331 (78.2%) delafloxacin vs 266/329 (80.9%) vancomycin + aztreonam; treatment difference -2.6% (95% CI -8.8, 3.6), noninferior (lower limit > -10%).

nct_ctgov.title: Delafloxacin Versus Vancomycin and Aztreonam for the Treatment of Acute Bacterial Skin and Skin Structure Infections

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind trial (RX-3341-303, IV with mandatory oral switch) of IV-to-oral delafloxacin (300 mg IV q12h or 450 mg orally q12h) vs vancomycin plus aztreonam in ABSSSI.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Objective response of >=20% reduction in lesion erythema vs baseline at 48 to 72 hours after initiation of therapy, with no evidence of clinical failure.
pivotal_trials.n: 850 randomized (423 IV/oral delafloxacin, 427 vancomycin plus aztreonam).
pivotal_trials.result: Objective clinical response 354/423 (83.7%) delafloxacin vs 344/427 (80.6%) vancomycin + aztreonam; treatment difference 3.1% (95% CI -2.0, 8.3), noninferior (lower limit > -10%).

nct_ctgov.title: Delafloxacin vs Vancomycin and Aztreonam for the Treatment of Acute Bacterial Skin and Skin Structure Infections

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=2%) were nausea (8%), diarrhea (8%), headache (3%), transaminase elevations (3%), and vomiting (2%); as a fluoroquinolone, associated with class serious adverse reactions (tendinitis/tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, CNS effects).
target_moa: Delafloxacin is a fluoroquinolone antibacterial that is bactericidal against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria by inhibiting bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV.

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for serious adverse reactions including tendinitis, tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, central nervous system effects, and exacerbation of myasthenia gravis (fluoroquinolone class).

advisory_committee.vote: These NDAs were not discussed at an advisory committee meeting as there were no specific issues that required input from the committee.

description.text: Added indication for treatment of Community-Acquired Bacterial Pneumonia (CABP) in adults

citations.quote: These Prior Approval supplemental new drug applications provide for the use of Baxdela (delafloxacin) 450 mg tablets and Baxdela (delafloxacin) 300 mg injection for the treatment of Community-Acquired Bacterial Pneumonia (CABP) in adults due to designated susceptible bacteria.

summary.text: BAXDELA received QIDP designation for ABSSSI (September 8, 2012) and fast track designation (December 18, 2012); based on the QIDP designation both NDAs received a priority review. It was a traditional (non-accelerated) approval based on two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 noninferiority trials.

In each trial, the lower limit of the 95% confidence interval for the treatment difference was greater than -10%, demonstrating that delafoxacin was noninferior to vancomycin plus aztreonam for the treatment of ABSSSI.

requirement.text: 3220-1: Conduct US surveillance studies for five years from the date of marketing to determine if resistance to delafloxacin has developed in organisms specific to the ABSSSI indication.

citations.quote: **3220-1:** Conduct US surveillance studies for five years from the date of marketing Baxdela to determine if resistance to delafloxacin has developed in those organisms specific to the ABSSSI indication in the label.

requirement.text: 3220-2: Conduct a tissue distribution study in pregnant rats treated during organogenesis with the oral and IV formulations of Baxdela with the excipient SBECD to assess distribution to the reproductive tract and developing fetus.

citations.quote: **3220-2:** Conduct a tissue distribution study in pregnant rats treated during the period of organogenesis with the oral formulation and with the intravenous formulation of Baxdela with the excipient sulfobutylether beta-cyclodextrin (SBECD) to assess the distribution of the drug substance to the reproductive tract and developing fetus.

requirement.text: 3220-3: If PMR 3220-2 shows greater fetal/maternal reproductive-tract exposure with the IV formulation, conduct an embryo-fetal developmental toxicology study in pregnant rats with the IV formulation of Baxdela with SBECD.

citations.quote: **3220-3:** If the results of the tissue distribution studies from PMR 3220-2 demonstrate greater exposure of the fetus / maternal reproductive tract to delafloxacin with the intravenous formulation, conduct an embryo-fetal developmental toxicology study in pregnant rats treated during the period of organogenesis with the intravenous formulation of Baxdela to identify possible effects of delafloxacin with the excipient sulfobutylether beta-cyclodextrin (SBECD) on fetal development during the period of organogenesis.
